prompt.en: A Yagi element is not connected to the feedline but is coupled by nearby RF fields. What is it called?

explanation.en: A parasitic element is energized by coupling from the driven element rather than direct feedline connection.

prompt.en: A roof-mounted quarter-wave vertical is used in the simple exam model. How is its horizontal pattern usually described?

text.en: It is strongest equally in all compass directions around the antenna
It has its main lobe only off one selected side of the car
It becomes directional only because the feedline is 50 ohms

explanation.en: In the Basic model, a quarter-wave vertical is omnidirectional in the horizontal plane; radials or the vehicle body provide the return side of the antenna system.

prompt.en: Why do two stacked identical antennas ideally add about 3 dB over one antenna?

text.en: Because the array concentrates the pattern in useful directions
Because the transmitters are allowed to exceed the same power limit
Because stacking cancels all feedline loss
Because the driven elements stop needing impedance matching

explanation.en: Stacking can add about 3 dB before losses by concentrating the combined pattern; it does not create transmitter power or remove feedline loss.
